title: Djoser depicted in the Saqqara Step Pyramid labyrinths, while later pyramids have no interior decoration
summary: Luke Caverns tells of Djoser depicted in the Saqqara Step Pyramid labyrinths, while later pyramids have no interior decoration, about Third Dynasty, c. 2670 BC at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: the sakara step pyramid down in those labyrinths below that there are depictions of the pharaoh joer up on the wall in his iconic like striding forward in a he said festival.

plain: Luke Caverns, a researcher, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that in the maze of tunnels beneath the Step Pyramid at Saqqara in Egypt, there are carvings of the early pharaoh Djoser striding forward during a festival. He contrasts this with the later pyramids, which he says have no decoration inside at all. In his telling, that difference raises the question of who built the later pyramids and why.
